welcome.title: Welcome to Ferry
welcome.desc: Ferry runs locally, scanning your AI coding tool sessions and unifying them in one view. No login required, no data uploaded.

wizard.highlightBrowse: Browse local sessions from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and more in one place
wizard.highlightHandoff: Migrate sessions across agents, or copy a resume instruction and let any agent take over
wizard.highlightUsage: Track token usage and estimated cost to understand your own habits
wizard.appearanceDesc: Theme and language apply immediately; both can be changed anytime in Settings.
wizard.toolsDesc: Ferry found these AI coding tools on this machine. After you start the scan it reads their session records; new sessions are picked up automatically.
wizard.handoffTitle: Sessions can ferry to any agent
wizard.handoffDesc: That's where the name comes from: carrying a session, context and all, from one agent to another.
wizard.handoffResume: Resume elsewhere: copy a /ferry-resume instruction into any agent with the skill installed — it reads the history, writes a takeover summary, and carries on.
wizard.handoffMigrate: Native migration: written in the target agent's own format, with an impact preview (kept / degraded / lost) first; the source session stays read-only.
wizard.scanDescReading: Parsing session metadata tool by tool — once this finishes, the session list is ready.
wizard.scanReadingHint: Reading… full-text indexing starts right after
wizard.scanDescIndexing: The session list is ready — enter anytime; full-text search completes as indexing progresses.
wizard.scanUnavailable: Index progress is unavailable right now; you can enter — indexing continues in the background.
wizard.confirmBody: {{indexed}} / {{total}} sessions indexed. Entering now doesn't affect browsing or organizing; search results complete as indexing progresses.
wizard.confirmBodyNoProgress: Index progress is unavailable, but browsing and organizing are unaffected; search results complete in the background.
wizard.integrationDesc: Install the ferry command-line tool and its companion skill in one click, so Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and others can search, read, resume, and migrate sessions. You can skip this — it's always available under Settings → Agent integration.
wizard.integrationHint: Only local symlinks and skill files are installed; no agent's session data is touched.

guide.railBody: The top half navigates modules (Overview, Sessions, Ask Ferry) and can be reordered by dragging; Pinned sits right under Sessions. The bottom half lists scopes by agent, favorite project, and tag — click one to see only those sessions, click it again to go back to all. Favorite projects can be dragged to reorder too.
guide.sidebarToggleBody: This title-bar button (or ⌘⇧S) hides the navigation rail and the resource pane together, leaving only the detail view for focused reading; click again to bring them back.
guide.overviewBody: Session count, token usage, estimated cost, and active-day streaks at a glance, switchable by tool and time range. Below: how your go-to model shifts over time and a 52-week activity heatmap.
guide.searchBody: Jump to any session by title, project directory, or command — full-text search over session content works too. Search and filter controls keep the same spot in the resource pane across modules.
guide.displayBody: Grouping, time window, only-with-sub-sessions and only-with-migrations live here; change any of them and a dot lights up on the button. Which slice of sessions you are looking at is not here — that is the scope in the sidebar.
guide.contextMenuBody: Right-click a session row to pin, archive, tag, or rename it, or favorite its project into the sidebar; you can also resume it in the terminal, migrate it to another agent, or copy its ID and resume command from here. ⌘-click to multi-select, then archive, tag, or delete in bulk.
guide.handoffBody: Click this button and it splits in two: the left copies the resume command for the original agent's terminal; the right copies a /ferry-resume instruction (also in the context menu) — paste it into any coding agent with the ferry-resume skill and it reads the history, writes a short takeover summary, and carries on. Nothing is written to any agent's store, so it works even when a native migration is refused (for example when the target does not support being migrated into).
guide.detailBody: The detail view renders the full session tree, including subagent conversations and image previews, with a context-usage chip at the top. From the top-right you can refresh, resume the conversation in your terminal, or copy the resume command or resume instruction; edits show a diff first, back up before applying, and can always be rolled back.
guide.scopeBody: Long sessions can be truncated at a turn with "Migrate up to here", carrying over only what came before; preview the migration impact before delivering. If verification fails, it rolls back automatically and leaves nothing behind.
guide.migrateBody: Move a session to another agent that supports being migrated into. Before writing, Ferry shows the impact: what's kept natively, what degrades, and what's lost. Confirm and it writes in the target agent's native format, then hands you a resume command to paste into your terminal. Migrated sessions are labeled with their origin in the session detail, and the source session stays read-only throughout. Cursor is not a migration target — use resume elsewhere instead.
guide.askferryBody: Let the built-in agent answer questions across sessions and run housekeeping tasks. When it's working in the background or needs your input, its rail icon lights up a badge; while browsing a session you can also summon it from the floating panel.
guide.integrationTitle: Let your coding agents use Ferry
guide.integrationBody: Settings → Agent integration installs the ferry command-line tool and its companion skill in one click, so Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and others can search, read, and migrate sessions and report usage. When an update is available, a download button appears at the end of this row — one click updates and restarts.
